What slows automotive teams down

We begin with the moments where people wait, repeat work, or lose context. Then we automate the predictable part and keep judgment with the right person.

  • Leads arrive from too many places

    OEM lead portals, the website, Meta and Google lead forms, marketplace dealer panels, missed calls and walk-ins each land in a different inbox or on a personal phone. Evening and weekend enquiries wait for the next shift, and buyers who hear nothing book a test drive elsewhere.

  • Follow-up depends on who is on the floor

    Consultants keep prospects in their own phones and notebooks. When someone is on leave or leaves the dealership, the history goes with them, and managers cannot see which leads were called, quoted or dropped.

  • Buyers chase delivery dates and RTO paperwork

    Waiting periods, allotment, loan disbursal, insurance, registration and HSRP fitment are tracked across the DMS, spreadsheets and phone calls. Buyers call again and again for updates and hear different answers from different people.

  • Workshop approvals stall the bay

    Technicians find additional work, but reaching the owner for approval takes calls that go unanswered. Vehicles sit half-finished, delivery promises slip, and verbal approvals turn into billing disputes later.

  • Owners drift to other workshops

    Free services end, warranties lapse and owners move to local garages. Reminders sent on fixed dates ignore how much each vehicle is driven, and nobody calls the owners who quietly stop coming.

  • Documents and money decisions need care

    Dealerships handle Aadhaar, PAN, RC copies, loan papers and insurance details, and make pricing, valuation and credit referral decisions. The DPDP Act, CMVR dealer rules, IRDAI and RBI requirements and TRAI messaging rules all shape what automation may do.

Every enquiry answered, qualified and booked for a test drive

All lead sources feed one queue linked to your DMS or CRM. Each enquiry gets an immediate WhatsApp reply where the buyer has opted in, a short qualifying flow, an assigned consultant with a response timer and an offer of test-drive slots. Managers see which sources turn into test drives and bookings, and every price, discount, exchange value and finance answer comes from a person.

What changes

  • Faster first responses, including evenings and weekends
  • Fewer leads lost between sources, shifts and personal phones
  • More enquiries reach a test drive, because booking takes one tap
  • Managers see which sources produce bookings, not just lead counts
  1. 1

    Pull every lead into one queue

    Connectors read OEM lead portal exports, website forms, Meta and Google lead forms, marketplace dealer panels, IVR missed calls and click-to-WhatsApp chats, remove duplicates by mobile number and record the source, model and consent captured on each form.

    nn8nMAMeta AdsGAGoogle Ads
  2. 2

    Acknowledge and qualify in minutes

    Opted-in buyers receive an approved WhatsApp template and a short flow asking model, fuel or variant, purchase timeframe, exchange and finance interest. Free-text questions are classified, and anything about price or offers is left for the consultant.

    WBWhatsApp Business PlatformACAnthropic Claude
  3. 3

    Assign and start the clock

    Rules route each lead by brand, branch, model and language to an available consultant, create the enquiry in the DMS or CRM and alert the team leader in Slack when the first call is not logged within the agreed window.

    ZCZoho CRMnn8nSSlack
  4. 4

    Offer test-drive slots

    The buyer picks a showroom or home test drive from slots tied to the demo fleet calendar, receives reminders with the location and documents to bring, and can reschedule in one tap.

    WBWhatsApp Business PlatformSSupabase
  5. 5

    Follow up until a decision

    A follow-up cadence prompts the consultant with the next action and the history so far. Automated nudges stop when the buyer books, declines or replies STOP, and lost reasons are captured for review.

    nn8nZCZoho CRM
  6. 6

    Measure source to booking

    A dashboard joins lead source and media spend with first response time, test drives, bookings and lost reasons by consultant and branch, reconciled with the DMS each week.

    MPMicrosoft Power BIGAGoogle Analytics 4

  7. People decide

    The assigned sales consultant makes the first call and owns the conversation, and team leaders reassign breached leads. Prices, discounts, exchange values and finance answers come only from people. The sales manager approves templates, qualifying questions and routing rules before launch and after every change.

A clear delivery rhythm

Five phases with named deliverables, client inputs, and review points. Most teams start with a focused pilot.

  1. 1

    1–2 weeks

    Discover

    We walk the journey with sales consultants, the finance and insurance desk, evaluators, registration staff, service advisors and drivers, at the showroom and workshop or by video. We map every lead source and document handoff, check what the DMS and OEM portals allow, and review consent wording and current messaging practice.

  2. 2

    1–2 weeks

    Design

    We design conversation flows, templates, routing and approval rules, document checklists and data flows. Price lists, discount limits, valuation rules and insurance processes stay with your managers; we encode the rules they approve.

  3. 3

    2–4 weeks

    Build

    We build the integrations in n8n and the agreed tools against test data or a DMS sandbox, set up consoles for consultants, advisors and coordinators, the consent log and dashboards, and document every connection and credential owner.

  4. 4

    1–2 weeks

    Validate & launch

    We test with consultants, advisors and registration staff, run scripted edge cases such as duplicate leads, opt-outs, price questions, declined estimates and document mismatches, fix what fails and launch at one showroom or workshop before any wider rollout.

  5. 5

    Ongoing, with monthly reviews

    Operate & improve

    We monitor failed messages, template quality ratings, missed response timers and model accuracy, review KPIs with your managers each month, and change templates, rules and prompts only through an approved change process. New branches and brands are added from the same playbook.

First pilot: Five-week lead response and test-drive pilot at one showroom

Start with one showroom or brand. Its main lead sources feed one queue, opted-in buyers get an immediate WhatsApp acknowledgment and a short qualifying flow, consultants receive assigned leads with first-call timers, and test drives are booked against the demo fleet. We compare first response time and lead-to-test-drive rate with the weeks before, using your own DMS or CRM data.

  • One showroom or brand with its main lead sources connected
  • Acknowledgment, qualification and test-drive templates approved by Meta and your sales manager
  • Routing and first-call alerts to the team leader during agreed hours
  • Consent log and a daily report of unanswered or failed messages
  • Baseline and pilot comparison of response time and test-drive rate

Know whether it is working

Proposed measures, agreed with your team before launch, with a source, owner, and review cadence.

Lead first response time
Elapsed time from a lead's arrival in any source to the first meaningful reply or logged call, reported by source, branch and staffed versus unstaffed hours.
Lead-to-test-drive rate
Share of qualified leads in a period that complete a test drive or test ride, by source and model.
Test-drive-to-booking conversion
Share of completed test drives followed by a booking within the agreed window, by consultant and model.
Booking-to-delivery cycle time
Median days from booking receipt to handover, split into waiting for allotment and time spent on dealer-side milestones such as finance, insurance and registration.
